title: Visible absorbing decompositions and uniqueness of invariant probabilities
summary: We identify the measurable absorbing obstruction to uniqueness of invariant probability measures for a Markov kernel. Ordinary absorbing decompositions obstruct global irreducibility and recurrence, but not necessarily uniqueness: an absorbing component may have full mass for no invariant probability. We prove that a Markov kernel has more than one invariant probability if and only if it admits a visible absorbing decomposition, namely two disjoint absorbing sets, each having full mass for an invariant probability.
